concepts.name: WEO Publication: Nature, Frequency, and Institutional Context
key_dimensions: Published twice a year (April and October) with interim updates in January and July — trap: not quarterly
Distinction between WEO as a flagship publication vs. IMF's other flagship reports (Global Financial Stability Report, Fiscal Monitor)
Role of the IMF Research Department in producing WEO vs. governance bodies like the Executive Board
WEO as a surveillance tool under IMF's Article IV mandate

concepts.name: WEO GDP Growth Projections: Methodology and Measurement Choices
key_dimensions: Use of both Market Exchange Rate (MER) and Purchasing Power Parity (PPP) for aggregating global GDP — UPSC trap on which method shows India/China larger share
Difference in global growth figures when MER vs PPP weights are used
Base year revisions and rebasing effects on historical data comparisons
Distinction between real GDP growth vs nominal GDP in WEO reporting

concepts.name: PPP vs Market Exchange Rate in WEO: Implications for Country Rankings
key_dimensions: India's GDP rank changes significantly under PPP (3rd) vs MER (5th) — frequent UPSC data point
Why WEO uses PPP for international comparisons of living standards but MER for financial flows
Balassa-Samuelson effect and its relevance to PPP divergence in developing economies
IMF's International Comparison Program (ICP) as the source of PPP data used in WEO

concepts.name: WEO Country Classification System: Advanced, Emerging, and Developing Economies
key_dimensions: Three-tier classification: Advanced Economies, Emerging Market and Developing Economies (EMDEs), Low-Income Developing Countries (LIDCs)
Criteria for classification — not solely per capita income; includes export diversification, financial integration (trap: different from World Bank income classification)
India's classification as an EMDE despite being top-5 economy by PPP — common confusion point
Overlap and divergence with World Bank, UN, and OECD country groupings

concepts.name: WEO's Role in IMF Article IV Consultations and Surveillance
key_dimensions: Article IV of IMF Articles of Agreement mandates bilateral surveillance — WEO aggregates this into multilateral surveillance
Distinction between bilateral surveillance (Article IV), multilateral surveillance (WEO/GFSR), and financial sector surveillance (FSAP)
How WEO projections influence IMF lending conditionalities and program design
Spillover Reports and WEO as tools for systemic risk identification

concepts.name: Global Growth Forecast Revisions: Causes and Policy Implications
key_dimensions: Factors triggering downward revisions: supply chain shocks, geopolitical conflicts, monetary tightening cycles
Concept of 'synchronized slowdown' vs 'divergent recovery' in WEO narratives
How WEO revisions influence G20 policy coordination and fiscal space discussions
Difference between 'baseline scenario' and 'downside/upside risk scenarios' in WEO

concepts.name: Inflation Forecasting in WEO: Global Inflation Dynamics
key_dimensions: WEO distinction between headline inflation and core inflation in cross-country analysis
Role of commodity price assumptions (oil, food) embedded in WEO inflation forecasts
Concept of 'last mile' disinflation — WEO's framing of sticky services inflation post-COVID
Divergence between advanced economy and emerging economy inflation trajectories in WEO analysis

concepts.name: Debt Sustainability Analysis (DSA) in WEO Framework
key_dimensions: WEO's tracking of global public debt as % of GDP — distinction from IMF's separate Fiscal Monitor
Concept of debt-to-GDP ratio thresholds and 'debt overhang' as used in WEO
Difference between gross debt and net debt in WEO country tables — trap for India's debt figures
WEO's treatment of contingent liabilities and off-budget financing in debt assessments

concepts.name: Current Account Balance and External Sector Analysis in WEO
key_dimensions: WEO's External Sector Report as a companion publication — distinction from WEO itself
Concept of 'global imbalances' — surplus (China, Germany) vs deficit (USA) economies in WEO framing
How WEO treats India's current account deficit trajectory and remittance inflows
Relationship between WEO current account projections and IMF's REER/NEER assessments

concepts.name: WEO Special Chapters and Analytical Essays: High-Yield Themes
key_dimensions: Each WEO issue contains 2-3 analytical chapters on cross-cutting themes — e.g., climate and growth, digitalization, informality
Recent high-relevance themes: Geoeconomic fragmentation, AI and productivity, green transition costs
How WEO analytical chapters feed into G7/G20 policy communiqués
Distinction between WEO analytical chapters and separate IMF Working Papers/Staff Discussion Notes

concepts.name: Geoeconomic Fragmentation and Trade in WEO Analysis
key_dimensions: WEO's quantification of costs of trade fragmentation — estimated long-run GDP loss of up to 7% in extreme scenarios
'Friend-shoring' and 'near-shoring' as concepts analyzed in WEO for supply chain rewiring
WEO treatment of technology decoupling and its differential impact on EMDEs vs Advanced Economies
Linkage between WEO fragmentation analysis and IMF's position on WTO reform

concepts.name: Climate Change and Green Transition in WEO Projections
key_dimensions: WEO's incorporation of carbon transition risks into growth forecasts — physical risk vs transition risk distinction
IMF's Climate Change Indicators Dashboard vs WEO's macroeconomic climate integration
WEO analysis on carbon pricing as a fiscal tool and its GDP growth trade-offs
Difference between WEO's climate treatment and World Bank's 'Groundswell' or IPCC reports — UPSC overlap trap

concepts.name: Poverty and Inequality Metrics in WEO vs Complementary IMF Reports
key_dimensions: WEO's limited direct coverage of poverty — primarily a growth/macro report (trap: not a poverty-focused report like World Bank's Poverty and Prosperity Report)
Gini coefficient and income inequality discussed in WEO analytical chapters but not headline tables
IMF's separate work on 'inclusive growth' through Fiscal Monitor vs WEO's macro framing
WEO's treatment of K-shaped recovery and distributional consequences of monetary tightening

concepts.name: WEO Data and the IMF World Economic Outlook Database
key_dimensions: WEO Database as a publicly accessible repository — distinction from IMF's IFS (International Financial Statistics) and BOP Statistics
Frequency and variables covered: GDP, inflation, unemployment, current account, fiscal balance for 190+ countries
Vintage data concept — how WEO database preserves historical forecast vintages for research
Limitations: WEO data relies on national statistical systems; quality varies — IMF's SDDS and e-GDDS standards as related concepts

concepts.name: IMF Growth Forecasts vs Other Institutions: Convergence and Divergence
key_dimensions: Comparison of IMF WEO forecasts with World Bank Global Economic Prospects, OECD Economic Outlook, and UN WESP — UPSC trap on which body publishes which report
Systematic optimism bias in IMF forecasts — academic literature critique and IMF's own IEO evaluations
How IMF WEO forecasts for India compare with RBI, CSO/NSO, and ADB projections — divergence reasons
Role of IMF's Independent Evaluation Office (IEO) in assessing WEO forecast accuracy

concepts.name: Recession Definition and WEO's Treatment of Global Recession
key_dimensions: IMF/WEO's definition of global recession: global growth below 3% (not the standard two-quarter rule used nationally) — critical UPSC trap
Distinction between technical recession (two negative quarters) and IMF's per capita income-based global recession threshold
WEO's identification of global recessions: 1975, 1982, 1991, 2009, 2020 — only five episodes post-WWII
How WEO differentiates between 'hard landing,' 'soft landing,' and 'no landing' scenarios

concepts.name: Fiscal Space and Government Finance Statistics in WEO
key_dimensions: WEO's use of 'fiscal space' concept — defined as room for expenditure increase or tax reduction without endangering debt sustainability
Distinction between WEO fiscal data and IMF's Fiscal Monitor — WEO has aggregate tables, Fiscal Monitor has deeper analysis
WEO treatment of India's fiscal consolidation path, fiscal deficit targets, and general government vs central government distinction
Automatic stabilizers vs discretionary fiscal policy framing in WEO policy recommendations

concepts.name: Monetary Policy Transmission and Central Bank Actions in WEO Framework
key_dimensions: WEO's analysis of global monetary policy synchronization — 'most synchronized tightening cycle in decades' post-2022 framing
Concept of 'higher for longer' interest rate environment and its spillover effects on EMDEs as analyzed in WEO
WEO's treatment of currency depreciation pressures on EMDEs during US Fed tightening cycles
Distinction between WEO's monetary analysis and IMF's Global Financial Stability Report (GFSR) on financial stability risks

concepts.name: Downside Risks and Uncertainty Quantification in WEO
key_dimensions: WEO's 'fan chart' methodology for representing forecast uncertainty — GDP growth probability distributions
Standard risk categories in WEO: financial stability risks, geopolitical risks, climate risks, policy uncertainty
Concept of 'balance of risks' — WEO frequently flags risks as 'tilted to the downside' — implications for policy
WEO's use of scenario analysis (e.g., pandemic resurgence scenario, financial stress scenario) vs baseline projections

concepts.name: India-Specific Data Points in WEO: Recurring UPSC Focal Areas
key_dimensions: India's growth rate projections — frequently cited as 'fastest growing major economy' in WEO; conditions and caveats attached
India's position in WEO GDP rankings under PPP vs MER — and when India may surpass Japan/Germany
WEO's assessment of India's structural reforms, demographics dividend, and infrastructure investment as growth drivers
WEO warnings on India-specific risks: fiscal consolidation needs, food inflation vulnerability, current account sensitivity to oil prices
